The memory-limit test uses :erlang.spawn_opt/2 with [:monitor, max_heap_size: %{size: ..., kill: true, error_logger: false}], asserting a real :DOWN/:killed message.

Cross-checked those primitives against the real REQ-155/REQ-156 mechanisms in lib/letflow/engine/lua/executor.ex (lines 70-146, 232-427: Task.Supervisor.async_nolink + Task.yield + Task.shutdown(:brutal_kill) for REQ-155; :erlang.spawn_opt/2 + max_heap_size for REQ-156) -- confirmed the test file uses the same real BEAM primitives (plain Task.async instead of the supervised async_nolink is an acceptable simplification for a unit test; the kill mechanism itself -- Task.shutdown(:brutal_kill) / max_heap_size kill -- is identical, not a fake stand-in). Sandbox.new(max_instructions:) is the real REQ-154 mechanism (sandbox.ex lines 267-268 pass it straight into the underlying Lua VM options).
